resources.string: aOS on the Mac now takes requests only when this computer signs them, with a key it gets when you pair. Show the pairing code on the Mac and paste its link here.
This computer loses the connection until the Mac wakes up again (open the lid or press a key). The workspace and your agents pause meanwhile.
This computer talks to your Mac over SSH with a key that never leaves it.
aOS on your computer
Confirming isn\'t available on this computer. Set up Windows Hello, or choose another way in Settings > This computer.
This code is from a newer aOS. Update aOS on this computer.
This computer makes its own key. Only its public half goes to the Mac.
Pair only with your own Mac. aOS on the Mac adds this computer\'s key to your user\'s SSH keys there.
How this computer reaches it
On the go through aOS\'s own Tailscale. After pairing, set it up on this computer too, with the same Tailscale account.
On the go through the Tailscale app. This computer needs it too, signed in with the same account (or aOS\'s own Tailscale, in Settings > Connection).
Only on the same network: elsewhere this computer doesn\'t reach the Mac.
This computer accepts the Mac only with exactly this key, now and later.
Name of this computer
This computer now reaches your Mac by itself whenever aOS runs.
The Mac didn\'t answer. Check that this computer is on the same network as the Mac and that the pairing code is still shown.
The Mac\'s answer wasn\'t understood. Update aOS on the Mac and on this computer.
Pair again to keep approving from this computer.
Update aOS on the Mac to see the workspace from this computer.
The Mac no longer accepts this computer. Pair again in aOS on the Mac.
The Mac isn\'t reachable. Elsewhere, set up aOS\'s Tailscale on this computer: Settings > Connection.
The Mac isn\'t reachable, and aOS\'s Tailscale on this computer isn\'t connected (Settings > Connection).
The Mac isn\'t reachable. Elsewhere, switch on Tailscale on this computer (the Tailscale app, or aOS\'s Tailscale in Settings > Connection).
This computer
SSH key of this computer
This computer forgets the Mac. To remove its key from the Mac too, open aOS on the Mac and remove it from the paired devices.
Sign-in requests and help requests from this Mac no longer reach this computer.
To log in to another computer with this computer\'s key, add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys there. The public key isn\'t secret.
They stay in your Bitwarden account. aOS on your Mac signs in to it with Bitwarden\'s own command line tool; this computer never talks to Bitwarden.
aOS on your Mac then gets exactly that login from Bitwarden and types it into the workspace. Neither this computer nor the Mac keeps it.
This computer reaches your Mac over SSH (the Mac\'s Remote Login), with a key made on this computer that never leaves it. The Mac\'s key is checked every time.
The Mac account name and password for its screen stay on this computer, encrypted, and only go to the Mac\'s screen sharing.
aOS\'s own Tailscale on this computer is Tailscale\'s open source code (tailscale.com), under the BSD 3-Clause License.
Apache MINA SSHD, Compose Multiplatform, Kotlin and kotlinx, JNA, JmDNS, and JediTerm by JetBrains (dual licensed LGPL-3.0 or Apache-2.0, used under Apache-2.0).
This computer tries the same network first, then the tailnet, then the Mac\'s name on the network.
Tailscale app on this computer
Your Mac uses the Tailscale app. On this computer the Tailscale app, signed in with the same account, reaches it too; so does aOS\'s own Tailscale below.
aOS\'s Tailscale on this computer
No VPN and no Tailscale app needed. aOS only reaches your Mac through it, and nothing on this computer is reachable in your tailnet. Its keys stay in aOS\'s folder on this computer.
aOS can bring Tailscale along on this computer too: no VPN, no extra app. You sign in once with your Tailscale account, the same as on the Mac.
Signed in. The tailnet\'s admin still has to approve this computer in the Tailscale admin console.
Sign Out removes this computer from the tailnet and deletes its Tailscale keys here.
Sign out of Tailscale on this computer?
This computer leaves your tailnet. Elsewhere it then reaches the Mac only through the Tailscale app, if it has it.
They keep running when the connection drops, also with aOS closed, and this computer picks up where it left off. End the ones you no longer need.
Open on this computer
Kept on this computer, encrypted for your user account, and read only after you confirm it\'s you. It only goes to the Mac\'s screen sharing.
Set up Windows Hello or choose another way to confirm in Settings > This computer.
Screens in the window\'s size

The workspace takes the window\'s shape: aOS resizes its display. Your own Mac keeps its size on the desktop (high performance video isn\'t played here). More resolution gives more room and less sharpness.
Requests that arrive while aOS\'s window is closed or hidden show as notifications of this computer.
aOS asks you to confirm it\'s you when it starts and when it comes back after a while.
aOS is locked
